facts.text: Chelas began as a rural parish, but the 1960s saw large social‑housing projects that welcomed migrants from Portugal’s former African colonies.
The Chelas metro stop sits on Lisbon’s Red Line, linking the city’s eastern suburbs to the historic city centre.
At the intersection of Avenida Doutor Augusto de Castro and Rua Engenheiro Rodrigues de Carvalho, the Chelas station borders the Instituto Superior de Engenharia de Lisboa.
Chelas enjoys excellent public‑transport links, with Oriente Station nearby serving as a major hub for trains, buses, and the metro.
Just a short walk from Chelas is the Oceanário de Lisboa, one of Europe’s largest aquariums, drawing marine‑enthusiasts worldwide.
The Chelas station’s design was crafted by architect Ana Nascimento, featuring installation art by plastic artist Jorge Martins.
